chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from Umar ibn Yazid said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man said, 'I will sit in my house, pray, fast, and worship my Lord, Exalted and Glorified is He; as for my provision, it will come to me.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'This is one of the three who will not have their supplication answered.'

key_terms.لَأَقْعُدَنَّ: I will sit/stay (indicating staying in one place)

ai.seo_question: Why is a man's supplication not answered if he thinks worship alone guarantees provision without working?
ai.summary: In the chapter on trade and livelihood (Bab al-Makasib), Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the passive attitude of those who equate mere ritual worship with sufficient reliance on God, neglecting the obligatory effort (kasb) to secure their sustenance. This hadith underscores the Shia principle that true tawakkul requires active engagement in the means of provision, distinguishing it from mere idleness or laziness disguised as devotion.
